steps.title: Prep the wedges
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Cut the potatoes into wedges. Toss them on a large baking tray with the oil, the smoked paprika (optional) and a pinch of salt.

steps.title: Roast the wedges
steps.text: Roast on the top shelf for 35 to 40 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.

steps.title: Make the filling
steps.text: While the wedges roast, slit the sausage skins and squeeze the meat into a bowl. Add the mixed herbs and a pinch of pepper and mix well with your hands.

steps.title: Roll the sausage rolls
steps.text: Unroll the pastry, cut it in half widthways, then wrap and chill (or freeze) the spare half. Cut the remaining piece in half lengthways to make two long strips. Shape the filling into two long sausages and lay one along the middle of each strip. Brush one long edge with milk, fold the pastry over and press the join with a fork to seal.

steps.title: Bake the sausage rolls
steps.text: Cut each strip into 3 rolls, put them on a lined baking tray, brush with milk and snip two small slits in the tops. Bake on the shelf below the wedges for 22 to 25 minutes until puffed and deep golden. The sausagemeat should be piping hot with no pink in the middle.

steps.title: Heat the beans and serve
steps.text: For the last 5 minutes, warm the beans in a small pan over a medium heat, stirring, until bubbling. Serve the sausage rolls with the wedges, beans and ketchup (optional).

changed: No onion to soften and no breadcrumbs, just herby sausagemeat; glazed with milk instead of egg.

ingredients.t: 1 small crackling joint (about 700g); leftovers make great sandwiches
2 teaspoons for the rind, plus extra

steps.title: Prep the pork and veg
steps.text: Heat the oven to 240°C (220°C fan). Pat the pork rind really dry with kitchen paper. Peel and halve the potatoes, halve the carrots lengthways and cut the broccoli into florets. Halve the onion, and peel, core and chop the apples.

steps.title: Start the pork
steps.text: Rub the meat (not the rind) with 1 teaspoon of oil and a pinch of pepper. Rub the rind with 1 teaspoon of oil, then 2 teaspoons of salt, working it into the scores. Sit it rind-side up on the onion halves in a roasting tin and roast on the top shelf for 25 minutes, until the rind starts to bubble. Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in salted water for 8 minutes, drain, leave to steam for 2 minutes, then shake in the colander to rough up the edges.

steps.title: Roast low and slow
steps.text: Turn the oven down to 200°C (180°C fan) and pour 100 millilitres of water into the pork tin, keeping the rind dry. Heat the remaining oil in a second tray for 5 minutes, tip in the potatoes and carrots with a pinch of salt and turn to coat. Roast both for 45 to 50 minutes, turning the veg once, until the pork juices run clear when the thickest part is pierced.

steps.title: Rest and make the apple sauce
steps.text: Lift the pork onto a board and rest, uncovered, for 15 minutes (foil softens the crackling). Turn the oven up to 220°C (200°C fan) and give the potatoes and carrots 15 minutes more until crunchy. Meanwhile, put the apples, butter and 2 tablespoons of water in a small covered pan over a medium-low heat for 8 to 10 minutes until the apples collapse, then mash with a fork.

steps.title: Make the gravy and broccoli
steps.text: Spoon the fat off the pork tin, add 300 millilitres of boiling water and scrape up the sticky bits. Strain into a small saucepan, pressing the onion. Whisk in the gravy granules over a medium heat and simmer for 1 to 2 minutes until thick. At the same time, boil the broccoli in salted water for 4 minutes until just tender, then drain.

steps.title: Carve and serve
steps.text: Carve the pork into thick slices and break up the crackling. Serve with the roast potatoes, carrots, broccoli, apple sauce and gravy poured beside (not over) the crackling.

changed: Fennel seeds and honey dropped and the steps merged into a plain, classic roast.

ingredients.t: 4 tablespoons (3 for the mash, 1 to glaze)

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.text: Chop the onion, cut the carrot into chunks and crush the garlic. Dissolve the stock cube in 200 millilitres of boiling water. Toss the beef with the flour and a pinch of salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a casserole or deep lidded pan over a high heat and brown the beef in two batches for 4 to 5 minutes each, until deep brown all over. Lift onto a plate.

steps.title: Simmer the filling
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium, add the onion and carrot and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and tomato purée for 1 minute, then pour in the ale, scraping the bottom. Add the stock, Worcestershire sauce and beef. Cover and simmer over a low heat for 1½ hours, stirring now and then, until the beef is tender and the gravy coats a spoon.

steps.title: Top the pie
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Spoon the filling into a small pie dish (about 1 litre) and leave to cool for 10 minutes. Brush the rim with milk, lay the pastry over, press the edges to seal and trim. Brush the top with milk and cut a small hole in the middle for steam.

steps.title: Bake the pie
steps.text: Put the pie on a baking tray and bake on the middle shelf for 25 to 30 minutes until puffed, deep golden and bubbling at the edges.

steps.title: Make the mash
steps.text: While the pie bakes, boil the potatoes in a large pan of salted water for 15 minutes until tender. Drain, leave to steam for 2 minutes, then mash with the butter, 3 tablespoons of milk and a pinch of salt until smooth.

steps.title: Cook the broccoli and serve
steps.text: For the last 4 minutes, boil the broccoli in salted water until just tender, then drain. Serve the pie with a big spoonful of mash, the broccoli and extra gravy from the dish.

changed: Pastry glazed with milk instead of a beaten egg and no dried herbs, so one less thing to buy.

steps.title: Prep the veg
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Cut the potatoes into bite-size chunks, the pepper into chunks and the red onion into wedges. Cut the chorizo into chunks and bash the garlic cloves.

steps.title: Start the potatoes
steps.text: Toss the potatoes in a large roasting tray with 1 tablespoon of oil, half the smoked paprika and a pinch of salt. Roast on the top shelf for 15 minutes to get a head start.

steps.title: Season the chicken
steps.text: While the potatoes roast, toss the chicken in a bowl with the remaining oil and paprika and a pinch of salt and pepper.

steps.title: Roast the chicken and chorizo
steps.text: Add the chicken, chorizo, pepper, onion and garlic to the tray and turn everything in the oil, sitting the chicken on top. Roast for 25 minutes, until the chicken is starting to brown and the chorizo releases its red oil.

steps.title: Add the tomatoes
steps.text: Scatter over the tomatoes and roast for 8 to 10 minutes more, until they burst and the potatoes are crisp. The chicken should be golden and cooked through, with no pink and clear juices.

steps.title: Wilt the spinach and serve
steps.text: Take the tray out and stir the spinach through the hot juices for 1 to 2 minutes until wilted. Serve straight from the tray.

changed: Honey and dried herbs dropped; the paprika and chorizo bring all the flavour.

ingredients.t: 1½ tablespoons for the chips, plus about 100ml for shallow-frying
½: a squeeze for the tartare, the rest in wedges

ingredients.swap: Spoon one portion of the lemony mayo into a separate dish before stirring in the gherkins.

steps.title: Prep everything
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Cut the potatoes into chunky chips, rinse, then pat them and the defrosted prawns really dry. Cut the lemon into wedges and finely chop the gherkins.

steps.title: Roast the chips
steps.text: Toss the chips on a large baking tray with 1½ tablespoons of oil and a good pinch of salt. Spread out in one layer and roast on the top shelf for 35 to 40 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.

steps.title: Make the tartare sauce
steps.text: While the chips roast, mix the mayonnaise with a squeeze from one lemon wedge and a pinch of pepper. Stir in the gherkins and chill until needed.

steps.title: Crumb the prawns
steps.text: When the chips have 15 minutes left, set out three plates: the flour seasoned with a pinch of salt and pepper, the beaten egg, and the panko. Dust each prawn in flour, dip in egg, then press firmly into the crumbs.

steps.title: Fry the scampi
steps.text: Heat about 100 millilitres of oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat until a crumb sizzles straight away. Fry half the prawns for 1½ to 2 minutes each side, until the crumb is golden and the prawns are pink all the way through. Drain on kitchen paper and repeat. Let the leftover oil cool before throwing it away.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Pile the chips onto plates with a sprinkle of salt and add the scampi. Serve with a pot of tartare sauce and the lemon wedges for squeezing.

changed: No capers, chilli powder or lemon zest; the tartare is just mayo, gherkins and a squeeze of lemon.

ingredients.swap: Make the marinade without the chilli flakes, coat all the chicken, then rub the flakes onto one portion's thighs only.

ingredients.t: 1 chicken stock cube in 300ml boiling water

ingredients.swap: Stir the hot sauce into half the mayo only and leave the rest plain.

steps.title: Prep and marinate
steps.text: Boil the kettle and make up 300 millilitres of stock with the cube. Finely chop the onion, dice the pepper and crush the garlic. In a bowl, mix the smoked paprika, chilli flakes, a third of the garlic, the lemon juice, 1 tablespoon of oil and the salt. Add the chicken thighs and turn to coat well.

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.text: Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil in a large, deep frying pan with a lid over a medium-high heat. Brown the thighs for 3 minutes each side until coloured but not cooked through. Lift onto a plate, leaving the oil and marinade bits in the pan.

steps.title: Fry the veg and rice
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium. Fry the onion and pepper for 3 minutes until starting to soften, then add the rest of the garlic for 1 minute. Stir in the rice and turmeric for 30 seconds so every grain is coated and yellow.

steps.title: Simmer the rice and chicken
steps.text: Pour in the stock and bring to a simmer. Sit the chicken thighs on top with any juices, cover and turn the heat to low. Cook for 15 minutes without lifting the lid.

steps.title: Rest off the heat
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes, until the rice is tender and the stock absorbed. Cut into the thickest thigh to check there is no pink and the juices run clear. Meanwhile, stir the hot sauce into the mayonnaise (both optional).

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Lift off the chicken, fluff up the rice with a fork and spoon into bowls. Top with the thighs and a drizzle of peri mayo (optional).

changed: Marinade is just paprika, chilli, garlic and lemon; no honey, dried herbs, sweetcorn or spring onions.

ingredients.swap: Make one portion of the salad without the cucumber, or serve the cucumber on the side.
Leave the lettuce off one plate.

ingredients.t: ½: a squeeze for the salad, the rest in wedges

steps.title: Get prepped
steps.text: Boil a full kettle. Quarter any larger potatoes so they are all a similar size. Slice the cucumber and separate the little gem leaves.

steps.title: Boil the potatoes
steps.text: Put the potatoes in a saucepan, cover with boiling water and add a pinch of salt. Simmer over a medium-high heat for 12 to 15 minutes, until a knife slides through easily.

steps.title: Fry the sea bass
steps.text: While the potatoes cook, pat the fish skin dry, make 2 or 3 shallow cuts in it and heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Lay the fillets in skin-side down, pressing flat with a spatula for 30 seconds. Season the flesh and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the skin is crisp and the flesh is nearly opaque. Flip, turn off the heat and leave for 1 minute.

steps.title: Butter the potatoes
steps.text: Drain the potatoes and return to the pan off the heat. Toss with the butter and a pinch of salt and pepper until glossy.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Toss the little gem and cucumber with 1 teaspoon of oil, a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lemon (optional). Share the potatoes between plates and top with the sea bass, skin-side up. Serve with the salad and lemon wedges (optional).

title: Crispy-Skin Sea Bass with New Potatoes & Salad
changed: No salted cucumber relish to make, so no red onion, rice vinegar or honey; just a simple lettuce and cucumber salad.

ingredients.swap: Keep the spring onions in a small bowl and stir them into one portion of potato salad only.

steps.title: Line the tin
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan and put a baking tray in to heat. Take the pastry out of the fridge 10 minutes before unrolling so it does not crack. Press it into a 20 centimetre loose-bottomed tart tin, letting the excess hang over the edge. Prick the base all over with a fork, line with scrunched-up baking paper and fill with baking beans or uncooked rice.

steps.title: Blind-bake the case
steps.text: Bake on the hot tray for 15 minutes until the edges are set. Lift out the paper and beans, then bake for 8 to 10 minutes more until the base looks dry and pale golden. Trim the overhanging pastry with a sharp knife.

steps.title: Fry the bacon
steps.text: While the case bakes, finely chop the onion, cut the bacon into thin strips and grate the cheddar. Fry the bacon and onion in a dry frying pan over a medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes, until the bacon is light golden and the onion is soft. Tip onto kitchen paper to drain.

steps.title: Fill and bake the quiche
steps.text: Whisk the eggs and cream in a jug with a good pinch of pepper; the bacon brings enough salt. Scatter the bacon and onion over the pastry case, then the cheddar. Pour in the egg mix and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until golden on top with a slight wobble in the centre.

steps.title: Make the potato salad
steps.text: Once the quiche is in the oven, put the potatoes in a saucepan of cold salted water. Bring to the boil and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes until a knife slides in easily, then drain and leave to steam-dry for 10 minutes. In a large bowl, mix the mayonnaise and mustard with a pinch of salt, fold in the warm potatoes and scatter over the spring onions (optional).

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Leave the quiche in its tin for 10 minutes so it sets and slices cleanly. Cut into 4 and serve 2 slices each with the potato salad and little gem leaves (optional).

changed: No garlic, butter or lemon; the bacon fries in its own fat and the potato salad is just mayo and mustard, with spring onions optional.

ingredients.swap: Leave the cabbage off one plate.
Leave the lettuce off one plate.

steps.title: Prep the veg
steps.text: Heat the grill to medium-high and line the grill pan with foil. Coarsely grate the apple (skin on) and the carrot. Finely shred the red cabbage.

steps.title: Shape the burgers
steps.text: In a bowl, mix the pork mince, grated apple, panko and Worcestershire sauce with a pinch of salt and pepper. With damp hands, shape into 2 patties about 2 centimetres thick and a little wider than the buns. Press a shallow dip in the middle of each so they stay flat. Chill for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Make the slaw and sauce
steps.text: While the burgers chill, mix 2 tablespoons of the mayonnaise with a pinch of salt in a bowl and toss in the red cabbage and carrot. In a small bowl, stir the rest of the mayonnaise with the mustard for the burgers.

steps.title: Grill the burgers
steps.text: Brush the patties with the oil and grill for 7 to 8 minutes on each side until golden. They are ready when there is no pink in the middle and the juices run clear.

steps.title: Melt the cheese
steps.text: Lay the cheddar over the burgers and grill for 1 minute until melted. Move them to a plate to rest. Toast the cut sides of the buns under the grill for 30 to 60 seconds, watching closely.

steps.title: Build and serve
steps.text: Spread the mustard mayo over the bun bases and add the little gem. Top with the cheesy burgers and the lids. Serve with the slaw on the side.

changed: No egg or lemon; all the apple goes in the burgers and the slaw is just cabbage, carrot and mayo.

ingredients.swap: Leave the cabbage off one plate.

steps.title: Rub the ribs
steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan. Mix 2 teaspoons of the smoked paprika with 1 teaspoon of salt and a good grind of pepper. Pat the ribs dry and rub the mix all over, mostly on the meaty side.

steps.title: Slow-bake under foil
steps.text: Lay the ribs meaty-side up in a roasting tin and pour 100 millilitres of water around them. Cover tightly with foil, sealing the edges. Bake for 1 hour 30 minutes until the meat is tender and starting to pull back from the bones.

steps.title: Prep the wedges
steps.text: About 15 minutes before the ribs are ready, cut the potatoes into chunky wedges, skin on. Toss on a large baking tray with the oil, the remaining ½ teaspoon of paprika and a pinch of salt, and spread out in a single layer.

steps.title: Crisp the ribs and roast the wedges
steps.text: Take the ribs out and turn the oven up to 200°C fan. Move the ribs to a foil-lined baking tray and pour away the juices. Put the ribs on the top shelf for 10 minutes until the rub looks crusty. Put the wedges in below and roast for 35 to 40 minutes, turning halfway, until golden.

steps.title: Glaze the ribs
steps.text: Turn the ribs bony-side up, brush with a third of the BBQ sauce and roast for 10 minutes. Flip, brush with half the remaining sauce and roast for 10 minutes more. Brush on the last of the sauce and roast for 5 minutes until sticky and dark at the edges. Meanwhile, mix the mayonnaise with a pinch of salt and toss in the red cabbage and carrot for the slaw.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Rest the ribs for 5 minutes, then cut between the bones. Serve with the wedges and slaw.

changed: Rub is just paprika, salt and pepper and the glaze is straight BBQ sauce; the slaw is cabbage, carrot and mayo.

ingredients.swap: Stir the sweetcorn into half the tuna mix only.
Make one portion of the salad without the lettuce, or serve the lettuce on the side.

steps.title: Get prepped
steps.text: Heat the grill to high. Put the sweetcorn in a sieve and pour over a kettle of boiling water to defrost it, then drain well. Grate the cheddar, chop the little gem and halve the tomatoes.

steps.title: Make the tuna mayo
steps.text: Drain the tuna well, pressing out the water with a fork. Mix with the mayonnaise, sweetcorn and a good grind of black pepper.

steps.title: Toast the bread
steps.text: Lay the bread on a baking tray and grill for 1 to 2 minutes until golden. Turn over, thinly butter the untoasted side and grill for 1 minute more.

steps.title: Grill the melts
steps.text: Spread the tuna mix over the buttered side, right to the edges. Pile the cheddar on top. Grill for 3 to 4 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and golden in patches.

steps.title: Dress the salad and serve
steps.text: While the melts grill, toss the little gem and tomatoes with the oil and a pinch of salt. Cut the melts in half and serve 2 slices each with the salad.

changed: No red onion, jalapeños or cucumber; just tuna, sweetcorn and mayo with a simple lettuce and tomato salad.

ingredients.swap: Leave the lettuce off one plate.

steps.title: Get prepped
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Cut the sweet potato into wedges, skin on. Drain and rinse the beans, then pat them dry on kitchen paper. Slice the spring onions.

steps.title: Roast the wedges
steps.text: Toss the wedges on a baking tray with 1 tablespoon of the oil and a pinch of salt. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and caramelised at the edges.

steps.title: Make the patties
steps.text: While the wedges roast, mash the beans in a bowl with a fork, leaving some chunky. Mix in the panko, egg, spring onions, chilli powder, paprika and a pinch of salt. With damp hands, shape into 2 patties about 2 centimetres thick. Chill for 10 minutes to firm up.

steps.title: Fry the burgers
steps.text: Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Fry the patties for 4 to 5 minutes on each side until crisp and hot through, turning carefully with a fish slice. Lay the cheddar on top for the last 2 minutes and cover the pan to melt it.

steps.title: Toast the buns
steps.text: Lift the burgers onto a plate. Wipe out the pan and toast the buns cut-side down over a medium heat for 1 minute until golden. Slice the avocado (optional).

steps.title: Build and serve
steps.text: Spread the yogurt over the bun bases and add the little gem. Top with the burgers, a few slices of avocado (optional) and the lids. Serve with the wedges.

title: Spicy Bean Burgers with Sweet Potato Wedges
changed: No cumin or garlic and no smashed avocado to make; sliced avocado is optional and the lime and coriander are gone.

ingredients.t: 3, sliced, whites and greens kept apart
ingredients.swap: Stir-fry the whites with the veg, but scatter the greens over one bowl only.

steps.title: Get prepped
steps.text: Put the kettle on. Sit the frozen prawns in a bowl of cold water for 10 minutes to defrost, then drain and pat dry. Slice the pepper and garlic, quarter the pak choi and slice the spring onions, keeping whites and greens apart. Mix the soy sauce and sweet chilli sauce in a small bowl.

steps.title: Cook the noodles
steps.text: Cook the noodles in a saucepan of boiling water for 4 minutes, or as the packet says, until just tender. Drain, rinse under cold water and toss with 1 teaspoon of the oil so they do not stick.

steps.title: Fry the prawns
steps.text: Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok or large frying pan over a high heat. Stir-fry the prawns for 2 to 3 minutes until pink all over. Tip onto a plate.

steps.title: Stir-fry the veg
steps.text: Add the pepper, garlic, ginger and spring onion whites to the wok and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add the pak choi and cook for 2 minutes more until the leaves wilt but the stalks stay crisp.

steps.title: Toss it all together
steps.text: Return the prawns to the wok with the noodles and sauce. Toss over a high heat for 1 to 2 minutes until the noodles are glossy and piping hot.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pile into bowls and scatter over the spring onion greens.

changed: Sauce is just soy and sweet chilli; oyster sauce, hot sauce, sesame oil and lime dropped.

steps.title: Get prepped
steps.text: Put the kettle on. Sit the frozen prawns in a bowl of cold water for 10 minutes to defrost, then drain and pat dry. Slice the onion and pepper and crush the garlic. Slice the pork into thin strips and toss with the hoisin. In a small bowl, mix the soy sauce, curry powder, black pepper and 2 tablespoons of water.

steps.title: Soak the noodles
steps.text: Put the noodles in a heatproof bowl and cover with just-boiled water. Soak for 6 to 8 minutes, or as the packet says, until soft but not mushy. Drain, rinse under cold water and drain well again.

steps.title: Scramble the eggs
steps.text: Heat 1 teaspoon of the oil in a wok or large frying pan over a medium heat. Pour in the eggs and stir for about 1 minute until just set, then tip onto a plate.

steps.title: Cook the pork and prawns
steps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in the wok over a high heat. Stir-fry the pork for 3 minutes, then add the prawns and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more, until the prawns are pink and the pork is cooked through with no pink. Tip onto the plate with the egg.

steps.title: Fry the veg
steps.text: Heat the remaining oil in the wok over a medium-high heat. Stir-fry the onion, garlic and ginger for 2 minutes until softened. Add the pepper and cook for 1 minute more.

steps.title: Toss and serve
steps.text: Add the noodles and sauce and toss with tongs until evenly yellow. Add the pork, prawns and egg and toss for 1 to 2 minutes until hot through, then serve.

changed: Pork stir-fried in strips with the prawns and the egg scrambled in the wok instead of a separate omelette; no honey, beansprouts or garnishes.

ingredients.t: a pinch, plus a pinch for the rice

steps.title: Get prepped
steps.text: Put the kettle on. Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally to make 4 thin steaks, then season with a pinch of salt. Spread 40 grams of the cornflour on a plate. Dissolve the stock cube in 100 millilitres of boiling water and juice the lemons.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice and put it in a saucepan with 300 millilitres of boiling water and a pinch of salt. Bring back to the boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Take off the heat and leave covered for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Make the lemon sauce
steps.text: Mix the remaining cornflour with a splash of the stock in a small saucepan until smooth. Stir in the rest of the stock, the lemon juice, honey and garlic. Simmer over a medium heat, stirring, for 2 to 3 minutes until glossy and the thickness of runny honey. Keep warm on the lowest heat.

steps.title: Fry the chicken
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat until a pinch of cornflour sizzles. Press the chicken into the cornflour to coat, shake off the excess and fry for 3 to 4 minutes each side until golden, crisp and cooked through with no pink. Drain on kitchen paper.

steps.title: Cook the broccoli
steps.text: While the chicken fries, cook the broccoli in a pan of boiling salted water for 3 to 4 minutes until just tender. Drain.

steps.title: Slice and serve
steps.text: Slice the chicken into strips and lay over the rice with the broccoli alongside. Spoon over the lemon sauce. Let the oil cool completely before binning it; never pour it down the sink.

changed: Shallow-fried in a simple cornflour coat instead of batter and a double deep-fry; no ginger, spring onion or lemon slices.

ingredients.swap: Keep them out of the wok and scatter over one portion only.

steps.title: Get prepped
steps.text: Boil the kettle and rinse the rice. Cut the chicken into pencil-thin strips and toss with 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce and a third of the garlic. Slice the pepper, cut the carrot into matchsticks and cut the spring onions into short lengths.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Tip the rinsed rice into a small pan with 300 millilitres of boiling water and a pinch of salt. Cover and cook on the lowest heat for 10 minutes. Take off the heat and leave covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

steps.title: Mix the sauce
steps.text: While the rice cooks, stir the remaining 2 tablespoons of soy sauce with the honey, rice vinegar and sweet chilli sauce in a small bowl.

steps.title: Coat and fry the chicken
steps.text: Toss the chicken strips in the cornflour until each one is dry and coated, then shake off the excess. Heat the oil in a wok or deep frying pan over a medium-high heat until a strip sizzles hard. Fry in 2 batches for 3 to 4 minutes until golden, crisp and cooked through. Drain on kitchen paper.

steps.title: Fry the veg
steps.text: Carefully pour off all but 1 tablespoon of the oil into a heatproof bowl (throw it away once cool). Stir-fry the remaining garlic, the pepper and carrot over a high heat for 1 to 2 minutes.

steps.title: Toss and serve
steps.text: Pour in the sauce and bubble for 30 seconds until syrupy. Add the chicken and spring onions and toss for 1 minute until coated. Serve on the rice.

changed: No egg white, sesame oil or chilli flakes; the chicken just goes in cornflour and a splash of rice vinegar replaces the lemon.

steps.title: Get prepped
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan and boil the kettle. Slice the pepper, cut the carrot into matchsticks, quarter the pak choi and grate the garlic. In a jug, mix 2 tablespoons of the sweet chilli sauce with the soy sauce, ginger paste and 3 tablespoons of water.

steps.title: Roast the salmon
steps.text: Put the salmon skin-side down on a lined baking tray and brush with 1 tablespoon of sweet chilli sauce. Roast for 12 to 15 minutes until it flakes easily and is opaque in the middle.

steps.title: Cook the noodles
steps.text: While the salmon roasts, cook the noodles in a pan of boiling water for 4 minutes until just tender. Drain and rinse under cold water.

steps.title: Stir-fry the veg
steps.text: Heat the oil in a wok or large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Stir-fry the pepper and carrot for 3 minutes. Add the garlic and pak choi for 1 to 2 minutes until the leaves wilt.

steps.title: Toss the noodles
steps.text: Pour the sauce into the wok and bubble for 1 minute. Add the noodles and toss for 1 to 2 minutes until coated and piping hot.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Divide the noodles between bowls and sit the salmon on top. Drizzle with the last tablespoon of sweet chilli sauce.

changed: Sauce is sweet chilli, soy and ginger; hoisin, lime and spring onions dropped.

ingredients.swap: Dip them in the simmering broth in a sieve for 1 minute and add to one bowl only.
Scatter over one bowl only.

steps.title: Get prepped
steps.text: Boil a full kettle. Halve the onion, leaving the skin on. Slice the spring onions (optional) and cut the lime into wedges.

steps.title: Char the onion
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over a high heat. Put the onion halves in cut-side down and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until blackened. Add the star anise for 30 seconds until fragrant.

steps.title: Simmer the broth
steps.text: Pour in 1.2 litres of boiling water and crumble in the stock cubes. Stir in the fish sauce, honey and ginger paste, then add the chicken. Bring to a gentle simmer, part-cover and cook for 25 minutes, skimming off any foam.

steps.title: Shred the chicken
steps.text: Lift the chicken onto a board and shred it with two forks. Fish the onion and star anise out of the broth with a slotted spoon. Taste and add a splash more fish sauce if needed.

steps.title: Cook the noodles
steps.text: Soak or boil the rice noodles in boiling water for 4 to 5 minutes (check the packet) until soft. Drain and rinse with hot water.

steps.title: Build the bowls
steps.text: Bring the broth back to a simmer and dip the beansprouts in for 1 minute. Divide the noodles, chicken and beansprouts between 2 deep bowls and ladle over the hot broth. Serve with lime wedges and spring onions (optional).

title: Vietnamese Chicken Pho with Rice Noodles
changed: Broth spiced with just star anise (no cinnamon or fennel) and no straining; coriander, chilli and hoisin garnishes gone.

ingredients.swap: Leave them out of the wok and sprinkle over one portion only.

ingredients.t: a small handful, chopped, to serve

ingredients.swap: Scatter over one portion only.

steps.title: Get prepped
steps.text: Boil the kettle. Cut the chicken into strips about 2 centimetres wide, season with a pinch of salt and toss in the cornflour until coated. Slice the pepper and chop the courgette and garlic. Chop the peanuts and slice the spring onions (both optional).

steps.title: Mix the peanut sauce
steps.text: Whisk the peanut butter and sweet chilli sauce with 2 to 3 tablespoons of warm water until smooth.

steps.title: Fry the chicken
steps.text: Heat 3 tablespoons of the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the chicken in one layer for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until golden, crisp and cooked through. Drain on kitchen paper.

steps.title: Cook the noodles
steps.text: Pour the boiled water into a pan and cook the noodles for 4 minutes until tender, then drain.

steps.title: Stir-fry the veg and noodles
steps.text: Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok over a high heat. Stir-fry the pepper and courgette for 4 to 5 minutes until charred in places. Add the garlic and chilli flakes for 1 minute, then the soy sauce and noodles, and toss for 1 to 2 minutes until glossy and hot.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pile the noodles into bowls and top with the crispy chicken. Drizzle over the peanut sauce and scatter with the peanuts and spring onions (optional).

title: Crispy Bang Bang Chicken Noodles with Peanuts
changed: One quick peanut sauce instead of two, no lime, honey or stock cube, and the courgette is simply chopped.

ingredients.t: ½ teaspoon, plus a pinch for the rice

steps.title: Get prepped
steps.text: Boil the kettle and rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Finely dice the onions and grate the garlic. Cut the chicken into bite-size chunks.

steps.title: Fry the onions
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan over a medium heat. Fry the onions with a pinch of the salt for 15 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden and browning at the edges.

steps.title: Toast the curry powder
steps.text: Stir in the garlic, ginger paste and curry powder. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant, adding a splash of water if it starts to catch.

steps.title: Reduce the tomatoes
steps.text: Add the chopped tomatoes and the rest of the salt. Simmer briskly for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until thick and jammy.

steps.title: Simmer the chicken and cook the rice
steps.text: Stir the chicken into the sauce until coated. Cover and cook over a medium-low heat for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until cooked through; add a splash of water if it gets too dry. Meanwhile, tip the rice into a small pan with 300 millilitres of boiling water and a pinch of salt. Cover and cook on the lowest heat for 10 minutes, then leave covered off the heat for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Fluff the rice with a fork and spoon onto plates with the bhuna alongside.

changed: Mild curry powder instead of five separate spices; butter, fresh coriander and green chilli dropped.

ingredients.t: 1 chicken or lamb cube in 250ml water

steps.title: Prep the ingredients
steps.text: Boil the kettle. Cut the potato into small chunks, leaving the skin on. Finely chop the onion and grate the garlic. Crumble the stock cube into 250 millilitres of just-boiled water and stir.

steps.title: Brown the lamb
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the lamb mince for 5 to 6 minutes, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until browned all over. Spoon away most of the fat, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the pan.

steps.title: Add the onion and curry powder
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic, ginger paste and curry powder and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

steps.title: Simmer with the potatoes
steps.text: Stir in the tomato purée, chopped tomatoes, potato and stock. Bring to a bubble, cover and simmer over a medium-low heat for 15 to 18 minutes, stirring now and then, until the potato is tender and the sauce is thick.

steps.title: Warm the naan
steps.text: While the keema finishes, heat a dry frying pan over a medium heat. Flick a few drops of water over each naan and warm for 1 minute each side until soft and lightly toasted. Wrap in a clean tea towel to keep warm.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Stir the spinach into the keema a handful at a time for 2 minutes until wilted, then season with salt. Serve with the warm naan and a spoonful of yogurt (optional).

changed: Just curry powder (no cumin seeds, turmeric or garam masala); mango chutney and coriander dropped, yogurt still optional.

ingredients.swap: Make one portion of the raita without the cucumber, or serve the cucumber on the side.

steps.title: Prep the ingredients
steps.text: Boil the kettle. Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold water until it runs almost clear, then leave to drain. Thinly slice the onion, grate the carrot and garlic, and cut the chicken into chunks. Crumble the stock cube into 350 millilitres of just-boiled water.

steps.title: Brown the chicken
steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide saucepan or casserole with a tight-fitting lid over a medium-high heat. Season the chicken with a pinch of salt and fry for 4 to 5 minutes, turning, until golden on most sides. It will finish cooking with the rice.

steps.title: Cook the onion and spices
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium and add the butter, onion and carrot. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring, until the onion is soft and turning golden. Stir in the garlic, ginger paste, garam masala and turmeric for 1 minute until fragrant.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Stir in the drained rice until every grain is glossy and coated in spice. Pour in the hot stock, stir once and bring to the boil. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 12 minutes without lifting the lid.

steps.title: Make the raita
steps.text: While the rice cooks, finely dice the cucumber and stir it into the yogurt with a pinch of salt. Keep in the fridge until needed.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat and leave it covered for 10 minutes. For the last 3 minutes, scatter the spinach on top and put the lid back on to wilt it. Fluff everything through with a fork and check the chicken is piping hot with no pink. Serve with the raita.

changed: No cumin seeds, lemon or coriander; the raita is just yogurt, cucumber and a pinch of salt.

ingredients.t: 8 tablespoons (2 for the marinade, 6 for the sauce)

ingredients.swap: Leave the onions off one plate.
Leave the lettuce off one plate.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Cut the chicken into chunks. In a bowl, mix it with the tikka paste and 2 tablespoons of the yogurt until well coated. Leave for at least 15 minutes, or cover and chill for up to 24 hours.

steps.title: Prep the salad and sauce
steps.text: Heat the grill to high. Shred the little gem, quarter the cherry tomatoes and thinly slice the red onion. Stir the garlic and a pinch of salt into the remaining 6 tablespoons of yogurt.

steps.title: Grill the chicken
steps.text: Thread the chicken onto skewers, or spread it out on an oiled, foil-lined baking tray. Grill on the top shelf for 12 to 15 minutes, turning halfway, until charred at the edges and cooked through with no pink.

steps.title: Warm the naan
steps.text: Move the chicken to a plate and cover to keep warm. Grill the naans for 1 to 2 minutes until puffed and lightly golden. Watch closely, as they catch quickly.

steps.title: Build the kebabs
steps.text: Lay each naan on a plate and pile on the lettuce, tomatoes, chicken and red onion. Spoon over the garlic yogurt sauce, then fold and eat.

changed: Just tikka paste and yogurt for the marinade; no pickled onion, lemon, cucumber, butter, chilli sauce or coriander.

steps.title: Prep the ingredients
steps.text: Finely chop 1 onion and cut the remaining half into chunks. Cut the pepper into chunks, the chicken into bite-size pieces and grate the garlic.

steps.title: Char the peppers
steps.text: Heat ½ tablespoon of the oil in a large deep frying pan or wok over a high heat. Fry the pepper and onion chunks for 4 to 5 minutes until charred at the edges but still with some bite. Tip onto a plate.

steps.title: Brown the onion
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium and add the remaining oil and the chopped onion. Cook for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden; add a splash of water if it catches.

steps.title: Cook the sauce
steps.text: Stir in the garlic, ginger paste and curry powder for 1 minute. Add the chopped tomatoes and tomato purée and turn the heat to medium-high. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until thick.

steps.title: Simmer the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken and stir to coat it in the sauce. Pour in 100 millilitres of water, cover and cook over a low heat for 15 minutes, stirring now and then.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Stir the peppers and onion back in and cook uncovered for 2 to 3 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce clings. Season with salt. Warm the naans in a dry frying pan for 1 minute each side and serve.

changed: Mild curry powder instead of six spices, peppers charred in the same pan first, and no yogurt, lemon, chillies or coriander.

ingredients.swap: Scatter the basil over one pizza only, or serve it on the side.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: In a large bowl, mix the flour, yeast and ½ teaspoon of salt. Add 160 millilitres of warm water and 1 tablespoon of oil and stir into a soft, slightly sticky dough. Knead on a lightly floured surface for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth and springy.

steps.title: Prove the dough
steps.text: Put the dough back in the bowl, cover with a clean tea towel and leave somewhere warm for 30 to 45 minutes, until puffy and nearly doubled. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 240°C (220°C fan) with two large baking trays inside.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Stir the garlic, mixed herbs, ½ tablespoon of oil and a pinch of salt and pepper into the passata. Tear the mozzarella into small pieces and pat dry with kitchen paper so the pizzas do not go soggy.

steps.title: Shape the bases
steps.text: Knock the air out of the dough and split it in two. On a floured surface, roll each piece into a thin round about the size of a dinner plate. Lay each one on a sheet of baking paper.

steps.title: Top the pizzas
steps.text: Spread half the sauce over each base, leaving a thin border. Scatter over the mozzarella and drizzle with the remaining ½ tablespoon of oil.

steps.title: Bake and serve
steps.text: Carefully slide each pizza, still on its paper, onto a hot tray. Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until the crust is golden and the cheese is bubbling and spotted brown. Scatter with basil leaves (optional), slice and serve.

changed: Parmesan dropped so mozzarella is the only cheese; basil stays optional.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast and ½ teaspoon of salt in a large bowl. Pour in 160 millilitres of warm water and 1 tablespoon of oil and bring together into a soft, slightly tacky dough. Knead on a floured worktop for 8 to 10 minutes until it is smooth and springs back when pressed.

steps.title: Prove the dough
steps.text: Return the dough to the bowl and cover with a tea towel. Leave in a warm spot for 30 to 45 minutes, until puffed up and nearly doubled. While it rises, heat the oven to 240°C (220°C fan) with two large baking trays inside.

steps.title: Prep the toppings
steps.text: Mix the passata with the garlic, mixed herbs, the remaining ½ tablespoon of oil and a pinch of salt and pepper. Drain the pineapple well and pat dry with kitchen paper. Tear the ham into bite-size pieces and tear the mozzarella.

steps.title: Shape the bases
steps.text: Punch the dough down and cut it in half. Roll each half on a floured surface into a thin round about the size of a dinner plate. Lift each base onto its own sheet of baking paper.

steps.title: Top the pizzas
steps.text: Spread the sauce over the bases, leaving a thin border. Scatter over the mozzarella, then dot the ham and pineapple evenly over the top.

steps.title: Bake and serve
steps.text: Slide the pizzas on their paper onto the hot trays. Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until the crust is golden and the cheese is bubbling. Cut into slices and serve.

changed: Mozzarella only, no second cheese, and the chilli flakes are gone.

steps.title: Prep the ingredients
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and put a large pan of salted water on to boil. Finely chop the onion and garlic. Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and season with half the mixed herbs, salt and pepper.

steps.title: Fry the chicken
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through with no pink. Tip onto a plate.

steps.title: Make the tomato sauce
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium and add the onion to the same pan. Cook for 5 minutes until soft, then stir in the garlic and tomato purée for 1 minute. Add the passata, the remaining herbs and a pinch of salt and simmer for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.

steps.title: Cook the pasta
steps.text: While the sauce simmers, cook the penne for 2 minutes less than the packet says, so it does not go soft in the oven. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.

steps.title: Assemble the bake
steps.text: Stir the pasta, chicken and a splash of the cooking water into the sauce. Tip into a medium baking dish and level the top. Scatter over the torn mozzarella and the cheddar (optional).

steps.title: Bake and serve
steps.text: Bake on the middle shelf for 20 minutes, until golden and bubbling at the edges. Leave to settle for 2 minutes, then serve.

changed: Mozzarella is the main cheese with cheddar optional; no parmesan or basil, and the chicken is fried in chunks.

ingredients.swap: Cook the sweetcorn in a small pan of boiling water for 3 minutes instead of with the pasta, and stir it into one half of the dish only before topping with cheese.

steps.title: Prep the ingredients
steps.text: Put a large pan of salted water on to boil and heat the grill to medium-high. Cut the broccoli into small florets, grate the cheddar and drain the tuna.

steps.title: Cook the pasta and veg
steps.text: Cook the penne as the packet says, adding the broccoli and sweetcorn for the last 3 minutes. Scoop out a small mugful of the cooking water, then drain everything in a colander.

steps.title: Make the cheese sauce
steps.text: While the pasta cooks, melt the butter in a medium saucepan over a medium heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the milk and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, whisking, until thick enough to coat a spoon.

steps.title: Mix the bake
steps.text: Take the sauce off the heat and stir in two-thirds of the cheddar, the mustard and some salt and pepper. Fold in the pasta, veg and tuna, adding a splash of cooking water if it is stiff.

steps.title: Grill and serve
steps.text: Tip into a heatproof baking dish and scatter over the remaining cheddar. Grill for 5 to 6 minutes until golden and bubbling, then serve straight away.

changed: No parmesan or cherry tomatoes; just cheddar sauce and cheddar on top.

steps.title: Prep the ingredients
steps.text: Finely chop the onion, slice the pepper and crush the garlic. Cut the chicken breast into bite-size pieces and slice the chorizo into half-moons. Crumble the stock cube into 350 millilitres of just-boiled water and stir to dissolve.

steps.title: Fry the chorizo
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan or sauté pan with a lid over a medium-high heat. Add the chorizo and fry for 2 to 3 minutes until it releases its red, smoky oil.

steps.title: Brown the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken to the chorizo oil with a pinch of salt. Fry for 4 to 5 minutes, turning, until golden on all sides. It will finish cooking in the sauce.

steps.title: Soften the veg
steps.text: Add the onion and pepper and cook for 4 minutes, stirring, until starting to soften. Stir in the garlic and smoked paprika and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.

steps.title: Simmer the pasta
steps.text: Pour in the chopped tomatoes and stock, then stir in the dried pasta. Bring to the boil, cover and simmer on a medium-low heat for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the pasta is tender and the chicken is white all the way through. Add a splash of water if it looks dry.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Season with salt and pepper. Spoon into bowls and top with the parmesan (optional).

changed: No cream or basil; it is a one-pan tomato pasta with optional parmesan.

ingredients.swap: Stir half the basil into the sauce as normal, and scatter the rest over one portion only at the end.

steps.title: Prep the ingredients
steps.text: Heat the grill to high and boil a full kettle. Crush the garlic and halve the cherry tomatoes. Tear the mozzarella into small pieces and pick the basil leaves.

steps.title: Make the tomato sauce
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Fry the garlic for 1 minute until fragrant but not brown. Add the passata, cherry tomatoes and half the basil, torn, then season. Simmer for 8 minutes until the tomatoes soften and the sauce thickens slightly.

steps.title: Cook the gnocchi
steps.text: While the sauce simmers, pour the kettle into a large saucepan over a high heat and add a pinch of salt. Cook the gnocchi for 2 to 3 minutes until they float to the top. Drain well.

steps.title: Combine in the dish
steps.text: Stir the spinach into the sauce for 1 minute until wilted. Fold in the drained gnocchi so every piece is coated. Tip into a medium ovenproof dish and spread out evenly.

steps.title: Grill until bubbling
steps.text: Scatter the mozzarella over the top. Grill for 5 to 7 minutes until the cheese is melted, bubbling and golden in patches.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Leave to stand for 2 minutes. Scatter over the remaining basil, then spoon into bowls.

changed: No parmesan or chilli flakes; mozzarella and basil do the work.

ingredients.swap: Leave the lettuce off one plate.

steps.title: Prep the ingredients
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (or as the shell packet says). Finely chop the onion. Shred the lettuce, dice the tomatoes and grate the cheddar. Slice the avocado (optional).

steps.title: Brown the mince
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a high heat. Add the beef mince and fry for 5 to 6 minutes, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until well browned with no pink left.

steps.title: Season the mince
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium and add the onion. Cook for 4 minutes until soft. Sprinkle over the fajita seasoning and stir to coat, then pour in 75 millilitres of water and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until the mince is saucy but not runny.

steps.title: Warm the shells
steps.text: While the mince simmers, stand the taco shells on a baking tray. Warm them in the oven for 3 to 4 minutes until hot and extra crisp.

steps.title: Build the tacos
steps.text: Spoon the mince into the warm shells. Top with lettuce, tomato, cheddar and a spoonful of soured cream, then the avocado (optional).

changed: Fajita seasoning instead of five spices and herbs; no garlic, jalapeños, coriander or lime, and avocado stays optional.

steps.title: Prep the veg
steps.text: Peel the sweet potato and cut into small, even chunks. Chop the onion and pepper. Drain and rinse both tins of beans. Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs clear.

steps.title: Soften the veg
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over a medium-high heat. Add the onion and pepper and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until soft and lightly coloured.

steps.title: Simmer the chilli
steps.text: Sprinkle over the chilli mix and stir to coat for 1 minute. Add the chopped tomatoes, both tins of beans, the sweet potato and 150 millilitres of water. Bring to the boil, then simmer on a medium-low heat with the lid half on for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sweet potato is tender and the chilli is thick.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: About 15 minutes before the chilli is ready, put the rice in a small saucepan with 300 millilitres of boiling water and a pinch of salt. Cover and cook on a low heat for 10 minutes. Take off the heat and leave to steam, lid on, for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Taste the chilli and add a pinch of salt if needed. Serve over the rice with a spoonful of soured cream (optional).

title: Veggie Bean & Sweet Potato Chilli with Rice
changed: Chilli mix sachet instead of four spices, the sweet potato simmers in the pot instead of roasting, and no lime or coriander.

steps.title: Prep everything
steps.text: Trim any thick fat from the steak and slice it thinly against the grain. Slice the peppers and onion into thin strips. Grate the cheddar and slice the avocado (optional).

steps.title: Cook the peppers
steps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Cook the peppers and onion for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and charred at the edges. Tip into a bowl.

steps.title: Sear the steak
steps.text: Put the pan back on a high heat with the remaining oil. Add half the steak in a single layer and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring, until browned outside and just pink inside. Repeat with the rest.

steps.title: Add the seasoning
steps.text: Return the peppers and onion to the pan. Sprinkle over the fajita seasoning and stir to coat, add a splash of water and toss for 1 minute until everything is glossy.

steps.title: Warm the wraps
steps.text: Wipe out a second frying pan and set it over a medium heat. Warm the wraps one at a time for about 20 seconds per side until soft.

steps.title: Fill and serve
steps.text: Pile the steak and peppers into the wraps. Top with soured cream, cheddar and the avocado (optional), then roll up.

title: Steak Fajitas with Soured Cream & Cheddar
changed: Fajita seasoning instead of three spices, garlic and lime; avocado is optional and sliced, not smashed, and no coriander or jalapeños.

ingredients.swap: Make one portion of the salad without the cucumber, or serve the cucumber on the side.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Crush 2 garlic cloves into a bowl. Stir in 3 tablespoons of the yogurt, the tomato purée, smoked paprika and 1 teaspoon of salt. Add the chicken chunks and coat well. Chill for at least 20 minutes, or up to 24 hours. If using wooden skewers, soak 4 in cold water.

steps.title: Make the salad and sauce
steps.text: Dice the cucumber, quarter the tomatoes and thinly slice the red onion. Toss together with the juice of half the lemon, 1 teaspoon of oil and a pinch of salt and pepper. Mix the remaining yogurt with the last garlic clove and a pinch of salt.

steps.title: Thread the skewers
steps.text: Heat the grill to high. Thread the chicken and pepper pieces alternately onto 4 skewers. Lay them on a foil-lined baking tray brushed with the remaining 1 teaspoon of oil.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice. Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over a medium heat, stir in the rice, then add 300 millilitres of boiling water and a pinch of salt. Cover and cook on a low heat for 10 minutes, then rest off the heat, lid on, for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Grill the kebabs
steps.text: While the rice cooks, grill the skewers for 10 to 12 minutes, turning halfway, until charred at the edges. Check a thick piece: the chicken should be white all the way through with no pink.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Fluff the rice with a fork. Serve the kebabs on the rice with the salad and garlic yogurt alongside, and the other lemon half cut into wedges for squeezing.

changed: No grated onion or turmeric in the marinade, no orzo in the rice and no chilli flakes; plain buttery rice instead.

ingredients.t: ½ lamb or beef cube in 100ml water

steps.title: Prep and roast the aubergine
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan and line 2 baking trays with baking paper. Slice the aubergine into thin rounds, brush both sides with the oil and season with salt. Roast in a single layer for 20 minutes, turning halfway, until soft and golden. Meanwhile, peel and thinly slice the potatoes, finely chop the onion, crush the garlic and grate the parmesan. Crumble the half stock cube into 100 millilitres of just-boiled water.

steps.title: Make the lamb sauce
steps.text: Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the lamb mince for 5 minutes, breaking it up, until browned, then spoon off most of the fat. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic, cinnamon, mixed herbs and tomato purée for 1 minute. Add the chopped tomatoes and stock and simmer for 25 minutes until thick, not watery.

steps.title: Parboil the potatoes
steps.text: While the sauce simmers, cook the potato slices in a pan of boiling salted water for 5 to 6 minutes until just tender at the edges. Drain and leave to steam dry. Turn the oven down to 180°C fan.

steps.title: Make the white sauce
steps.text: Melt the butter in a small saucepan over a medium-low heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the milk, then simmer for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until thick enough to coat a spoon. Take off the heat, stir in half the parmesan and season.

steps.title: Layer the moussaka
steps.text: Lay the potato slices over the base of a medium ovenproof dish. Top with half the aubergine, all the lamb sauce, then the rest of the aubergine. Pour over the white sauce and scatter with the remaining parmesan.

steps.title: Bake and rest
steps.text: Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until deep golden and bubbling at the edges. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting so the layers hold together.

changed: No cumin and no egg beaten into the white sauce; prep and roasting merged so there are fewer steps.

ingredients.swap: Crumble the feta over one burger only.
Make one portion of the tzatziki without the cucumber, or serve the cucumber on the side.
Leave the lettuce off one plate.
Leave the tomatoes off one plate.

steps.title: Prep the ingredients
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C fan. Cut the potatoes (skin on) into wedges. Thinly slice the red onion. Coarsely grate the cucumber and squeeze out the liquid. Crush the garlic, separate the lettuce leaves and slice the tomatoes.

steps.title: Roast the wedges
steps.text: Toss the wedges on a baking tray with 1 tablespoon of oil, 1 teaspoon of the mixed herbs and a pinch of salt. Roast for 30 to 35 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp at the edges.

steps.title: Shape the burgers
steps.text: In a bowl, mix the lamb mince with the remaining mixed herbs, a pinch of salt and plenty of pepper. Shape into 2 patties about 2 centimetres thick and chill until needed.

steps.title: Make the tzatziki
steps.text: Mix the yogurt with the grated cucumber, garlic and a pinch of salt.

steps.title: Cook the burgers
steps.text: About 15 minutes before the wedges are ready, heat the remaining 1 teaspoon of oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the burgers for 5 to 6 minutes each side until browned and cooked through, with no pink in the middle. Rest for 2 minutes, and toast the buns cut-side down in the pan for 1 minute.

steps.title: Build and serve
steps.text: Layer lettuce and tomato on the bun bases, then add the burgers, crumbled feta, a spoonful of tzatziki and the sliced red onion. Add the bun lids and serve with the wedges.

title: Greek Lamb Burgers with Feta, Tzatziki & Wedges
changed: Feta crumbled on top instead of stuffed inside; no breadcrumbs, Worcestershire or lemon.
